been at Holmes Chapel Health Centre for about a year since moving to the area, and honestly, it’s been really frustrating. I know reception staff have a tough job, I’ve worked in health centres myself, so I try to be understanding, but it often feels like everything is a struggle.

From the start, even signing up felt like a burden. The front desk staff were rude and seemed uninterested in answering basic questions. It often makes you feel more like a nuisance than a patient.

Dealing with prescriptions has been another source of stress. My first new prescription wasn’t signed correctly, which is fine, mistakes happen, but I was only given one month instead of the two months I used to get at my previous surgery. When I asked about it, I got a curt email citing surgery policy. I understand rules exist, but the tone was unnecessarily rude, especially for a common antidepressant. On top of that, it’s frustrating having to spend an extra £60 a year because of this.

I also had a test for a condition a few months ago that came back clear. When my symptoms didn’t go away and I called, I was told nothing could be done over the phone and that I had to submit an e-consult. I understand the process, but the unwillingness to help over the phone felt rigid and unhelpful and it seems like a pattern.

Moving to a new area and dealing with a new surgery has been daunting, and overall it’s been a tough experience.

That said, I do want to say I’ve had one experience with a medical professional that was actually brilliant. Dr Marriott was absolutely fantastic, kind, understanding, empathetic, and kept my expectations grounded on what could be done to help.
